issues.legal_issue: Time limits and lapse consequences in the general land acquisition law do not govern the preliminary and final stages of acquisition under a self-contained planned-development law when that law provides its own scheme.
material_facts: A development authority issued a preliminary notification to acquire land for a planned urban layout.
The final declaration had not been issued for several years, and landowners argued that the acquisition should lapse by applying time limits from the general land acquisition law.
The planned-development statute contained its own acquisition procedure and consequences for failure to implement a scheme.
issues.conclusion: The general land acquisition law’s time limits, including the provisions governing the time for a declaration and lapse of acquisition, could not be imported into the planned-development statute. The authority’s acquisition was governed by that statute’s own scheme, including its provisions concerning implementation and default.
issues.legal_principle: The planned-development statute is a self-contained code. Under sections 15–19 and 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, read with section 36, provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 apply only insofar as applicable; its distinct time limits and default consequences, including sections 6 and 11A, do not become part of the planned-development statute. The Court relied on Offshore Holdings Private Limited v. Bangalore Development Authority (2011) 3 SCC 139, which approved the self-contained-code principle in Munithimmaiah v. State of Karnataka (2002) 4 SCC 326 and considered Bondu Ramaswamy v. Bangalore Development Authority (2010) 7 SCC 129.

predicates.planned_development_acquisition: A public authority undertook land acquisition as an incident of carrying out planned development.
predicates.special_law_has_its_own_acquisition_sche: The law governing the development project provided its own acquisition procedure and consequences for default.
predicates.challenge_relies_on_general_acquisition_: A party sought to invalidate or lapse the acquisition by relying on time limits in the general land acquisition law.

issues.definition: When a planned-development acquisition is governed by a law with its own acquisition scheme and a challenge relies on general acquisition time limits, those general time limits do not govern the special scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in completing a preliminary acquisition process does not justify quashing the preliminary notification where the delay arose amid inquiries into irregular proposed exclusions and the landowners contributed to the obstruction of the planned public development.
material_facts: A preliminary notification covered land for a planned urban layout, but a final declaration was delayed.
Proposals were made to exclude substantial areas after the preliminary notification, and public questions and inquiries followed concerning the proposed exclusions.

The Court found that the landowners had acted in collusion with influential persons and authorities in attempts to obtain exclusions, and that the challenged proceedings followed the inquiries and a notice that the matter would be reconsidered.
The High Court quashed the preliminary notification on account of delay.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary notification could not be quashed on the ground of delay in these circumstances. The landowners could not benefit from delay to which they had contributed, and the notification was upheld; the authorities were directed to proceed to the final declaration without further delay.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot take advantage of its own wrong. The time for implementation and the consequences of default under section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act relate to the statutory scheme and do not make a preliminary notification lapse merely because of delay. The Court relied on Offshore Holdings Private Limited v. Bangalore Development Authority (2011) 3 SCC 139 and distinguished the preliminary acquisition stage from the later implementation of a final scheme.

predicates.challenge_to_preliminary_acquisition_not: Landowners brought a proceeding seeking to invalidate a preliminary notice for a planned-development acquisition.
predicates.delay_arose_amid_inquiries_into_proposed: The process was delayed while authorities examined disputed proposals to exclude notified land from the acquisition.
predicates.landowners_contributed_to_obstruction: The landowners acted in a way that contributed to the delay or obstruction of the acquisition process.
predicates.acquisition_serves_planned_public_develo: The acquisition was intended to serve a public planned-development purpose.

issues.definition: When landowners challenge a preliminary acquisition notice after delay arising amid inquiries into proposed exclusions, contributed to by the landowners, and the acquisition serves planned public development, the delay does not invalidate the notice.

issues.legal_issue: Land included in a planned-development acquisition cannot be excluded through a process marked by suspected irregularity without accountability review, and the authority must continue the acquisition pending that review.
material_facts: Land had been included in the preliminary notification for a planned-development scheme.
After notification, officials proposed excluding substantial areas of the notified land, prompting questions in the legislature and public concern.
The government ordered inquiries into the proposed exclusions, but their results were not available to the Court.
The Court considered that the proposed exclusions appeared to have been made in connivance with influential persons.
issues.conclusion: The authority and government were directed to proceed with acquisition of the identified land without excluding it. The Court appointed an inquiry officer to determine the responsibility of officials involved in the attempted exclusions and directed the authorities to provide records and assistance for the inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Authorities must carry out the statutory mandate of planned development and may not frustrate its public purpose through irregular exclusions. The Court relied on the planned-development obligations under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, including its scheme and acquisition provisions, and on the public-interest principles applied in the judgment.

predicates.land_was_included_in_a_planned_developme: The land was covered by a preliminary notice for a planned-development project.
predicates.exclusion_was_proposed_after_notice: Officials proposed removing the land from the acquisition after the preliminary notice had been issued.
predicates.proposed_exclusion_was_under_inquiry_for: The proposed removal of land was questioned and was the subject of an inquiry into possible irregular conduct.

issues.definition: When land covered by a planned-development notice is later proposed for exclusion and that proposal is under inquiry for irregularity, the acquisition continues without exclusion and official responsibility is investigated.
